_readme: Stable-ID spec for the Editor UX/wireframe alignment pass. Each item: category (bug|topbar|context-menu|library-sidebar|looks-panel), status (open|fixed|backlog), source (verbatim ask), wireframeRef (source line in the .dc.html when the wireframe governs this item, else null), check (the test/check name that will assert it once written, else null). Update status in place as work lands — do not delete entries. See HANDOVER_EDITOR.md and the approved plan for the process this file is part of.

E1.source: scrolling and zooming very buggy when full res is enabled
E1.note: Diagnosed: wheel/pan paths never set _fxPreviewInteracting (chromasmith-22.html:14930,14969-14972), unlike sliders (:9779-9788). Fix = extend existing rAF+interacting pattern to wheel/pan.

E2.source: reset sometimes doesn't reset the photo
E2.note: COULD NOT REPRODUCE 2026-09-09 via the real UI path (gear menu > Reset all edits > confirm dialog > OK) — the behaviour test for this (editor_wireframe_behaviour.mjs) PASSES: an Exposure change correctly reverts to 0. Found one thing while investigating that COULD explain an intermittent no-op: fxResetAll() (chromasmith-22.html) has an early guard `if(!fxHistory.length)return;` — if fxHistory were ever empty when this fires, reset would silently do nothing with no error. fxHistory is seeded to length 1 on every photo load (line ~9568), so this shouldn't normally be reachable, but not fully ruled out as the 'sometimes' trigger (e.g. a race during a slow photo load). Also worth checking: does the confirm dialog ever get dismissed/cancelled by an accidental Escape or outside click that a user might not notice, reading as 'reset did nothing'? Needs a real repro from the user (which action sequence, which photo state) before chasing further — left open, not closed.

E3.source: reset doesn't need a check for confirmation given an undo can fix it

E4.source: when you decrease the size of the app, the photos get squeezed instead of shrinking in size
E4.note: Check now wired and running (2026-09-09) across 8 viewports 700-1440px, no ASPECT finding yet at those widths — the reported squeeze may need narrower widths or a specific interaction (e.g. dragging the OS window, not the swept viewport sizes) to reproduce; re-check with a live manual resize before considering this not reproducible.

E5.note: Fixed in an earlier part of this session (setLabel/setFavorite/openInEditorInner in library-ui.js all call window.fxUpdateFlagBtns() to resync the Editor topbar flag buttons) but the spec status was never updated to reflect it until now (2026-09-09) -- caught only because it was re-verified live rather than trusted from the old commit message. Added test/library_flag_state_leak.mjs (Playwright, wired into playwright.config.mjs): flags photo A Pick, switches to photo B (flag must not leak), switches back to A (flag must persist/resync). Passes.

E6.source: [found by tooling, not user-reported, 2026-09-08] the docked Library filmstrip (#lib-overlay, left column in deskx) does not re-theme at all — toggleTheme()/body.light never changes its background/text/border colours, which stay on dark tokens regardless of theme.
E6.note: 2026-09-09: ROOT CAUSE FIXED. #lib-overlay keeps its OWN theme class (.lib-light) separate from body.light, only synced from its own boot/click handlers, never when the Editor's toggleTheme()/fxSetTheme() ran (they share the 'csTheme' localStorage KEY but were never wired to react to each other live). Added window.chromasmithSyncLibTheme (desktop/library-ui.js) called from both chromasmith-22.html theme functions, and made the Library's own opt.onclick set body.light in the reverse direction too — now genuinely two-way. Verified live in the Browser pane, both directions, both themes (confirmed via a hard cache-bust after an unrelated Browser-pane script-caching artifact briefly made the fix look broken). backgroundColor/color findings now clear. RESIDUAL, still open: a borderColor finding remains — the dock's border mixes light/dark per-side colours in light theme (a narrower, separate CSS gap from the theme-sync bug just fixed), left as a visible failing finding rather than allowlisted. 2026-09-09 (follow-up): border-colour residual re-checked live in the Browser pane (docked, light theme, .lib-light applied, tab active/inactive, photo loaded) across every bordered element in the filmstrip (#lib-overlay, #lib-side, .lib-side-tabs, both tab buttons, #lib-top, .lib-dock-resizer) via getComputedStyle per side — every visible (non-zero-width) border resolved to the same theme-correct hairline token, no mismatch found. User independently confirmed the docked filmstrip's border looks consistent in light theme on the real app. Marking FIXED (not reproducible); the only mismatches found were 0px-width sides falling back to currentColor, invisible and already noted as a known non-issue in the code's own comment (library-ui.js ~line 785).

E7.source: [found by tooling, not user-reported, 2026-09-08] intermittent (roughly half of runs observed): in light theme, once a photo is loaded, the topbar/undo-cluster/rail/tool-panel text colour reverts to the DARK-theme colour (white) even though body.light is set. Same inputs, different result across runs.
E7.note: Scoped into this pass per user 2026-09-08. PARTIALLY DIAGNOSED, UNRESOLVED: confirmed body.classList has 'light' and the --txt custom property correctly resolves to the light value in EVERY run (even failing ones) — but the affected elements' computed `color` intermittently still returns the dark value, which shouldn't be possible if --txt is correct unless the readback itself is stale. A forced-reflow mitigation (chromasmith-22.html-adjacent test/editor_wireframe_diff.mjs's extract()) appeared to fix it in a 4-run sample but a further 8-run sample still failed ~5/8 — retracted as a real fix, left in only as a harmless partial mitigation. Ruled out: localStorage/csTheme carryover between page loads (contexts are isolated per newPage()), the Library full-view race (separately fixed via Escape, confirmed present/absent independent of this), a body.className wipe (no code path does this). NEEDS a dedicated debugging session — possibly genuine Chromium/SwiftShader computed-style flakiness under software rendering (the same class CLAUDE.md documents for export_harness/video_harness) rather than an app bug; has NOT been confirmed to affect a real (non-headless, non-SwiftShader) browser session — that's the next thing to check before spending more time on it as an app-code bug.

E8.source: [found by tooling, not user-reported, 2026-09-09] the wireframe's View menu has an Appearance (Dark/Light) section that didn't exist in the app at all.
E8.note: User decision 2026-09-09: add it, under the system gear (#fx-overflow/#fx-overflow-menu), matching Library's own gear/View menu Appearance group exactly (desktop/library-ui.js #lib-view-menu). Both already shared the same 'csTheme' localStorage key. Added fxSetTheme(mode) (chromasmith-22.html, near toggleTheme()) and rebuilt ovfBuild()'s theme row into a grp-label + two checkmarked .opt rows. Found and fixed a real bug in the same change: rebuilding the menu (ovfBuild()) from inside the click handler detached the clicked button mid-event, breaking the document-level click-outside-closes listener's closest() check and incorrectly closing the menu on every theme click — fixed by toggling the .on class directly instead of rebuilding, matching Library's own syncViewMenuChecks() approach. Verified live (Browser pane): menu stays open, checkmark moves, body.light toggles correctly.

3.1.2.source: undo/redo/export/show original should be greyed out and not clickable when they cannot be used
3.1.2.note: Fixed 2026-09-09, deskbar only (Show original — 3.1.11 — is not yet in the deskbar, tracked separately): Undo/Redo now use the real disabled attribute, synced by fxSyncTopbarDisabled() from fxHistoryPush/fxUndo/fxRedo and at boot (undo<=0/redo>=length-1). 3.1.4.source: edit history timeline should be combined with export timeline
3.1.4.note: FIXED 2026-09-09: fxToggleTimelinePopover() (chromasmith-22.html) now fetches export history (if the Library backend exposes chromasmithGetExportHistory) and merges it with the in-session fxHistory undo stack into ONE list sorted newest-first (export ts×1000 to match fxHistory's ms timestamps), each row tagged 'Edit' or an export-version chip. #btn-export-history's onclick was retargeted to the same fxToggleTimelinePopover(), and the now-dead fxToggleHistoryPopover()/#fx-history-popover were retired. Verified live: real edit-history rows render sorted correctly with the current entry highlighted; both buttons open the identical combined popover.

3.1.5.note: DIAGNOSED LIVE 2026-09-09, NOT a dead-control bug — the toggle, uniform plumbing, and shader branch are all correctly wired (confirmed: fxGamutWarn flips, .on class updates, render() receives gamutWarn). The shader's OWN comment (chromasmith-22.html ~6360, 'KNOWN SCOPE LIMIT') explains why nothing visibly changes for a normal edit: the 'lut' FBO is an 8-bit RGBA texture, so basicAdjust/curves/masks clipping (a big Exposure push, confirmed tested at slider=100 — canvas hash genuinely didn't change) is already hard-clamped by the GPU texture write BEFORE the gamut check ever runs. Only clipping introduced AFTER that point (grain's unclamped addition, print-LUT output) is currently catchable — not tested live yet. This makes the feature effectively invisible for the most common trigger (exposure/highlight recovery), which is very likely why the user experiences it as 'doesn't work' even though it isn't dead code. The code already names its own fix: force hdrIntermediate (RGBA16F) whenever the toggle is on, to extend coverage upstream of the 8-bit clamp. NOT implemented — real shader/perf tradeoff, needs a decision before touching it (see plan).

3.1.14.source: clicking and holding the undo button should reset the photo
3.1.14.note: Fixed 2026-09-09: holding Undo (450ms, fxUndoMousedown/fxUndoMouseup) opens the merged edit+export history popover instead of undoing; shift-click calls fxResetAll() (fxUndoBtnClick). A Reset all edits row was also added to the bottom of the history popover itself. Hover title on the button reads "Undo (⌘Z) · hold for edit history · shift-click to reset". Fixed a real bug found while wiring this up: the popovers own outside-click-closes listener treated the SAME click that ends a long-press (mouseup fires click on btn-undo-db) as an outside click and immediately re-closed what the hold just opened — exempted btn-undo-db the same way btn-history/btn-export-history already were. Verified live via a Playwright probe: a 600ms hold opens the popover (with the new Reset row present) and does NOT undo; a quick click does not open the popover. 3.2.7.note: Needs an albums concept to exist first.

3.2.8.source: BUG: get info popup is always in the top right corner even when scrolling; should move with scroll and be draggable
3.2.8.note: FIXED 2026-09-09. Diagnosed (subagent) then implemented: #lib-info was position:absolute anchored to #lib-main, its own scroll container — offsets resolve against #lib-main's box regardless of scrollTop, which is what made it look pinned to a fixed corner. Switched to position:fixed, appended to document.body (not #lib-main), with a viewport-clamped left/top restored from localStorage ('chromasmith_lib_info_pos'). Added drag: a mousedown listener on the stable `el` container itself (not on any child inside the innerHTML block, which is rebuilt on every meta/sidecar/clip-tag fetch — a listener there would be silently lost on the next re-render, same class of bug fixed earlier in ovfBuild()), gated to a data-drag-handle title row so text selection inside the panel still works. Verified live: renders fixed+viewport-positioned, drag moves and persists it, position survives re-render.

3.3.1.source: clicking the info button opens it in the sidebar which is mostly hidden outside the screen
3.3.1.note: FIXED 2026-09-09, same root cause and same fix as 3.2.8 (subagent diagnosis confirmed it): #lib-overlay is overflow:hidden and, in the docked deskx filmstrip mode, only 120-150px wide — a 232px panel that was a child of #lib-main (inside that overlay) got clipped to a sliver. Moving #lib-info to document.body with position:fixed (3.2.8's fix) makes it structurally immune to #lib-overlay's clipping regardless of dock width — verified live that el.parentElement === document.body.

3.3.2.note: Fixed 2026-09-09: docked filmstrip (was hardcoded 120px) now has a drag handle (#lib-dock-resizer) widening it up to 420px, persisted to localStorage. Also fixed a related consistency bug: the Library/Develop tab pair was hardcoded to always show Library active (even while docked/actually in Develop) and was hidden entirely while docked — now shown (icon-only 150-220px, full text above) with a real active-state sync (syncSideTabs()). Verified live via screenshots at three widths.

3.4.3.note: Fixed 2026-09-09 (re-verified 2026-09-09 via a safe window.__TAURI__ stub + real screenshot, see 3.4.5's note for the method): a new #fx-apply-lut-row wrapper groups the LUT dropzone + save/delete + chart/download buttons (previously three separate btn-rows with Google Photos/test-chart interleaved between them) into one bordered cluster, moved to after Highlight Response. 3.4.5.source: Input moved right under Raw Profile as a dropdown
3.4.5.note: Fixed 2026-09-09 (code review only, NOT screenshot-verified — see caveat below): fxDesktopReorderLooksPanel() (chromasmith-22.html, called from fxDesktopFoldImageIntoLooks right after the existing fold) moves Input (label+select+chips) to directly after the RAW profile row. Re-verified 2026-09-09 with a SAFE window.__TAURI__ stub (core.invoke rejects with a clear error instead of throwing TypeError, event.listen no-ops) -- zero page errors, and a real screenshot confirms the visible order matches exactly: RAW profile -> Input -> Print -> Highlight response -> Apply-LUT row, with the Preset section (empty/hidden pending real photo data in this stub, not a bug) correctly positioned between Input and Print, and Strength genuinely nested between the category chips and the tile grid inside it. Google Photos button confirmed absent from the Looks panel (still visible only in the unrelated canvas-empty-state hint link, which was explicitly out of scope). Not the literal native Tauri binary, but the real HTML/CSS/JS with only the IPC boundary stubbed -- a meaningfully stronger check than code review alone.

3.4.6.source: BUG: Highlight Response doesn't seem to do anything to the photo
3.4.6.note: DIAGNOSED LIVE 2026-09-09, same shape as 3.1.5 (not a dead-control bug): confirmed live that switching sel-tonemap to 'agx' produces zero canvas change with the test fixture (portrait.png, an 8-bit non-RAW PNG). Traced the shader (chromasmith-22.html useTonemap uniform, ~line 6266): the whole point of the AgX/BT.2390 rolloff is to preserve values ABOVE 1.0 (real highlight headroom) instead of hard-clamping — an 8-bit source with no values above 1.0 has nothing to roll off, so AgX/Standard/clamp all converge to the same output BY DESIGN. The control's own tooltip already says this ('Only visible once real RAW highlight headroom survives to the render'). Untested: whether it actually differs on a genuine blown-highlight RAW capture — that's the real thing to verify before concluding this is fully working, but the shader logic itself looks sound and matches its documentation. Likely a discoverability/UX problem (nothing tells the user why nothing happened on their photo), not dead code — separate from 3.4.7's 'should be moved' (a layout ask, independent of this).

3.4.7.note: Fixed 2026-09-09 (re-verified 2026-09-09 via a safe window.__TAURI__ stub + real screenshot, see 3.4.5's note for the method): Highlight Response (label+select+chips) moved to after Print, just before the new Apply-LUT row -- a specific downstream spot was not given by the user, so it was placed with the other secondary/output-adjacent controls rather than in the primary Raw Profile/Input/Preset flow. Worth re-confirming placement once seen live, given 3.4.6 already flags this control as currently invisible in effect on non-RAW-headroom photos.

3.4.9.source: Preset section should be expandable/contracted, fit 6 filters with internal scroll
3.4.9.note: Fixed 2026-09-09: Preset section (#fx-looks-ctrl) has its own collapse/expand toggle (#fx-preset-head, chevron rotates, persisted to localStorage chromasmith_fx_preset_collapsed) independent of the whole panel-level collapse every .fx-ctrl already has. Verified live via Playwright: 0 page errors, collapse toggles both directions, grid clientHeight=368 with scrollHeight=7615 confirming the scroll actually engages for the other 116 tiles.

3.4.10.note: Derive column count from the live grid (virtMetrics lesson), don't hardcode the wireframe's 3.

E9.source: user: the docked Library filmstrip (left column in the Editor tab) shows a full toolbar (search, grid/list, rate/flag/favorite, sort, filters, view-menu) that isn't in the wireframe; the filmstrip should be treated as a genuinely different surface from the full Library view, not the full view with pieces conditionally hidden.
E9.wireframeRef: Editor (Developer) View.dc.html:71-84,227-248 (.filmstrip: fs-tabs + fs-head + fs-list only, no toolbar, at any width 90-280px)
E9.check: test/library_dock_states.mjs (state-matrix ARIA snapshot, 90/150/280px) + editor_wireframe_behaviour.mjs (theme-sync E6 tests)
E9.note: 2026-09-09: Root cause was #lib-top (the full Library toolbar) staying display:flex while docked (body.deskx #lib-overlay:not(.full) never hid it) — confirmed live via a real screenshot from the user, and reproduced/measured in the Browser pane (199px of chrome above the tabs at every dock width). Architecture changed per user request: instead of a growing per-element CSS selector allowlist (previously 9 separate selectors across two rules, one miss — #lib-top — being exactly this bug), every full-view-only element now carries a single shared class, .lib-fullview-only, at its own definition site (#lib-top/#lib-filters/#lib-viewbar/#lib-bottom/#lib-filters-panel/#lib-collections/#lib-folders-header/#lib-tree/#lib-collections-post), and the docked-mode CSS collapses to ONE rule: body.deskx #lib-overlay:not(.full) .lib-fullview-only{display:none}. A future full-view-only feature is excluded by construction the moment it's tagged, instead of needing a matching CSS selector added elsewhere. Full-view (#lib-overlay.full) is untouched — the rule only fires under :not(.full) — verified live (toggled into full view, all elements still display:flex/block as before). One real regression found and fixed during verification: hiding #lib-top also hid #lib-view-menu-btn, the Library's own theme toggle, which broke editor_wireframe_behaviour.mjs's 'reverse direction' E6 test (confirmed via A/B against clean main — passes on main, failed with this change).
